target_customer: Mining companies, geotechnical and engineering consultancies, insurers and infrastructure owners that must assess ground stability and site risk
problem: Engineers who sign off on site safety must manually hunt through consultant, contractor and monitoring reports; early on the company sold satellite ground deformation monitoring to mines.
business_model: B2B software subscription and monitoring services; started as satellite monitoring studies and moved to the TRAIL AI platform
product_category: Satellite InSAR monitoring and AI risk analysis for mines and infrastructure

education: NIT Karnataka (started Mycopie there; degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC page; the page gives 2020 in his bio and 2021 elsewhere as the start.

founders.background_notes: Former professional hockey player turned geoscientist per the YC page; led ground monitoring systems used by mining customers.

founders.background_notes: YC page gives no last name; 14 years of software experience including AR/VR.

competitors.traction_then: Described as a worldwide leader in InSAR monitoring services

competitors.what: Geospatial platform with a mining ground stability monitoring case study
competitors.traction_then: Case study claims 60 percent monitoring savings for a mining client

technical_complexity.rationale: InSAR processing of satellite radar and later building a knowledge graph with AI agents over decades of site records requires specialist geoscience and data engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Domain expertise and site-specific data records are hard to copy; the InSAR service itself had several established providers.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established InSAR firms kept operating; no sourced case of an incumbent copying the TRAIL document analysis approach.

market_need_then: Mine and tailings safety carries regulatory and safety consequences; satellite InSAR for mining was an established method before 2022, per industry sources.

identity.logo: Wordmark; details not described by sources
identity.voice_and_tone: Evidence-first, tagline 'Traceable AI for billion-dollar builds'

branding.brand_signature: Traceability: every AI finding cites its source page and data point

brand_strength.rationale: Niche B2B brand with a clear traceability message, but no press on the brand and a name that is easy to confuse with Kore.ai.

pivots.from: Ground deformation monitoring and geotechnical studies using satellite data
pivots.to: TRAIL, an AI platform and agents over site records and monitoring data
pivots.why: The company says engineers kept hitting the same problem synthesizing reports; no exact date given.

outcome_analysis: KorrAI is active with about 20 people and works with large mining and insurance customers, including Zurich and AWS per its site. Disclosed funding is small, around 1.6M in 2022 plus grants, and a 2026 article says it is raising a seed round. It moved from satellite monitoring services to an AI platform called TRAIL. Domain founders and enterprise customers help, while capital remains limited.
notes: Funding totals conflict: Dealroom about 1.6M pre-seed (YC, ParticleX, SDTC plus Canadian Space Agency grants), CB Insights 1.03M over 10 rounds with a 0.26M grant in June 2025, Village 2.4M, FundedIQ 1.4M. The 1.6M figure with date Nov 2022 is from the YC page news line; stage not stated so 'other'. A Fondo article of 2026 says a seed round is being raised, not completed. Competitor sources are undated industry pages; these firms existed before 2022 but no source dated near the batch was found. Founding year inconsistent (2020, 2021, 2022). Location Toronto per YC, Halifax per Dealroom. Name origin not found.
